Chapter 10: The Ongoing Quest—God in a Global Age.
Think about how small the world feels these days. Technology lets us connect instantly, no matter where we live. Ideas and beliefs spread faster than ever, and because of that, our search for God has started to look a little different.
Picture a young woman in Mumbai. She’s scrolling through messages from friends all over the globe. In just one afternoon, she reads about Buddhist meditation, Christian prayer, and Sufi poetry. For her, faith isn’t just a label or a set path—it’s a journey. It’s the way she explores life’s deepest mysteries.
Religious traditions keep growing and changing, shaped by the questions and challenges of our time. Some communities try hard to protect their heritage, while others welcome new ways of thinking. The old lines between sacred and secular, between belief and doubt—they’re getting blurrier every day.
When global crises hit—like climate change, poverty, or violence—many of us turn to our faith for answers. We look for wisdom in ancient stories, but we also find hope in the courage of people who dream of a better world. Searching for God becomes a search for meaning, for connection, for hope itself.
But let’s be honest, the journey isn’t always smooth. Sometimes old wounds come back, and new conflicts appear. It can be tempting to retreat into what feels certain, to draw lines between “us” and “them.” Still, there’s always that call—to compassion, to justice, to love.
In the end, this quest for God is truly human. It’s shaped by our longing, our struggles, and that endless drive to find meaning in the mystery of life.
